bib.title: Large Dual Encoders Are Generalizable Retrievers

question: Can scaling up a dual encoder while keeping a single fixed-size dot-product bottleneck improve retrieval, especially out-of-domain generalisation?
hypothesis: Scaling the dual encoder size (not the bottleneck) improves generalisation, contrary to the belief that the dot-product bottleneck limits dual encoders.
contributions: GTR: T5-based dual encoders up to 4.8B with fixed 768-d bottleneck, multi-stage training
Scaling improves BEIR zero-shot, outperforming prior sparse and dense retrievers
Diminishing gains from larger embedding size
10% of MS Marco suffices for matching OOD performance

method.summary: Dual encoders initialised from the T5 encoder (Base to XXL, 110M to 4.8B) with a fixed 768-d mean-pooled embedding and cosine similarity, pre-trained on 2B web QA pairs then fine-tuned on MS Marco or NQ with hard negatives. Evaluated zero-shot on BEIR, with ablations on training stages, data amount, fine-tune set, pre-training strategy, bottleneck size and latency.
method.task: dense passage retrieval, zero-shot generalisation on BEIR

datasets.name: MS Marco

datasets.source: Kwiatkowski et al. 2019; hard negatives from Lu et al. 2021

datasets.name: BEIR

datasets.preprocessing: query/doc max length 64/512 tokens; Trec-News and Robust-04 doc 768; ArguAna query 512

models.name: GTR-Base

models.name: BM25, DocT5Query, DPR, ANCE, TAS-B, GenQ, ColBERT
models.architecture: sparse and dense baselines from BEIR

training.objective: in-batch sampled softmax with optional hard negatives, bi-directional (q-to-d and d-to-q)

inference.retrieval: cosine similarity of 768-d mean-pooled embeddings; ANN search mentioned generally

eval.protocol: BEIR zero-shot; no seeds or significance tests reported

results.claim: Scaling the T5 encoder from Base to XXL with a fixed 768-d dot-product raises zero-shot BEIR NDCG@10 from below BM25 to above it (XXL).
results.setup: BEIR, 18 datasets, MS Marco excluded from the average; GTR pre-trained on 2B community QA pairs then fine-tuned on full MS Marco with RocketQA hard negatives; 768-d embedding, mean pooling, cosine similarity
results.note: GTR-Base 0.416, Large 0.445, XL 0.453; Avg incl. MS Marco: XXL 0.457
results.table: Table 3, row Avg w/o MS Marco, column GTR-XXL

results.claim: GTR-Base zero-shot average is below BM25.
results.setup: BEIR, 18 datasets, MS Marco excluded from the average; GTR pre-trained on 2B community QA pairs then fine-tuned on full MS Marco with RocketQA hard negatives; 768-d embedding, mean pooling, cosine similarity
results.table: Table 3, row Avg w/o MS Marco, column GTR-Base

results.claim: Recall@100 shows the same trend: XXL above BM25.
results.setup: BEIR, 18 datasets, MS Marco excluded from the average; GTR pre-trained on 2B community QA pairs then fine-tuned on full MS Marco with RocketQA hard negatives; 768-d embedding, mean pooling, cosine similarity
results.table: Table 8, row Avg w/o MS Marco, column GTR-XXL

results.claim: Fine-tuning the pre-trained GTR-XXL on 10% of MS Marco gives zero-shot score at least equal to using all of it, while in-domain drops.
results.metric: NDCG@10 zero-shot avg w/o MS Marco
results.setup: BEIR zero-shot; 10% of training queries kept with their positive and hard-negative passages; GTR-XXL
results.note: MS Marco in-domain GTR-XXL 0.379 (10%) vs 0.442 (100%). Abstract: 'it only needs 10% of MS Marco supervised data to match the out-of-domain performance of using all supervised data'
results.table: Table 4, row Zero-shot 10%, column GTR XXL

results.claim: Without pre-training, XXL fine-tune-only trails full GTR; pre-training only is far behind.
results.metric: NDCG@10 zero-shot avg w/o MS Marco (GTR-FT / GTR-PT / GTR, XXL)
results.table: Table 5, rows XXL (zero-shot block), columns GTR-FT, GTR-PT, GTR

results.claim: Larger bottleneck gives minimal gain from 768 to 4096 while model size consistently helps.
results.setup: Fine-tuned on MS Marco only (no pre-training); six OOD datasets (BioASQ, DBPedia-entity, NQ, HotpotQA, Fever, SciFact); dims 256/768/2048/4096; values only in Fig 7
